symptom: PC on VLAN 30 cannot reach anything, including its own gateway.
topology_note: PC connected to switchport Gi0/3, intended to be access VLAN 30.
show_output:
show interfaces Gi0/3 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Switchport assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN cannot ping each other despite correct IP addresses.
topology_note: Both PCs on VLAN 20, connected via two switches with a trunk link between them.
show_output:
show interfaces trunk
Port   Mode   Encapsulation  Status    Native vlan
Gi0/1  auto   n-802.1q      trunking  1
Allowed VLANs: 1,10,40
expected_fault: VLAN 20 not included in the allowed VLAN list on the trunk

symptom: New VLAN created but devices assigned to it still can't communicate; VLAN not visible on other switch.
topology_note: VTP domain configured across 3 switches; new VLAN 60 added only on Switch A.
show_output:
show vlan brief (Switch B)
VLAN 60 not listed
expected_fault: VLAN not propagated due to VTP mode mismatch (Switch A in transparent mode)

symptom: Voice VLAN phone fails to register; data still passes fine from the same port.
topology_note: Switchport Gi0/7 configured for PC + IP phone, using voice VLAN 15.
show_output:
show interfaces Gi0/7 switchport
Voice VLAN: none
expected_fault: Voice VLAN not configured on the switchport

symptom: PC can ping its own IP and other PCs on the same subnet, but not the default gateway.
topology_note: PC 192.168.10.5/24 gateway should be 192.168.10.1 on VLAN 10 SVI.
show_output:
show ip interface brief
Vlan10  unassigned  YES manual  administratively down  down
expected_fault: VLAN 10 SVI is administratively down

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway even though gateway interface shows up/up.
topology_note: PC configured with gateway 192.168.20.1; SVI Vlan20 is up.
show_output:
PC ipconfig
Default Gateway: 192.168.20.254
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway configured on the PC (mismatched with actual SVI IP)

symptom: Intermittent gateway reachability; ping succeeds sometimes and times out other times.
topology_note: PC and gateway on VLAN 30; duplicate IP suspected.
show_output:
show ip arp
Internet  192.168.30.1  0  0011.2222.3333  ARPA  Vlan30
Internet  192.168.30.1  0  00aa.bbcc.ddee  ARPA  Vlan30
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address on the network causing ARP conflict

symptom: All PCs on a subnet lose gateway access after a switch reboot.
topology_note: VLAN 40 SVI configured on a stacked switch; HSRP not in use.
show_output:
show ip interface brief
Vlan40  192.168.40.1  YES NVRAM  down  down
expected_fault: SVI line protocol down, likely no active ports assigned to VLAN 40 after reboot

symptom: New PC gets a 169.254.x.x address instead of an IP from the DHCP server.
topology_note: PC on VLAN 30; DHCP server is centralized on VLAN 10 via IP helper.
show_output:
show running-config interface Vlan30
(no ip helper-address configured)
expected_fault: Missing ip helper-address on VLAN 30 SVI, so DHCP requests never reach the server

symptom: Some PCs on a VLAN get IP addresses, others do not.
topology_note: DHCP pool for VLAN 20 configured with a small address range.
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool VLAN20
Current index: 192.168.20.20
Total addresses: 20
Leased: 20
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted, no addresses left to lease

symptom: PC receives an IP address from the wrong subnet.
topology_note: Two DHCP pools misconfigured with overlapping option settings.
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool
Pool VLAN10: network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: DHCP pool for VLAN10 mistakenly configured with VLAN20's subnet

symptom: PC fails to renew IP lease and drops off the network periodically.
topology_note: DHCP lease time set very short for testing and never changed back.
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool VLAN30
Lease: 0 days 0 hours 2 minutes
expected_fault: DHCP lease time set too short, causing frequent renewal failures under load

symptom: PC can ping a server by IP but cannot reach it by hostname.
topology_note: PC configured with a DNS server IP that does not respond.
show_output:
PC ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 192.168.100.200 (unreachable)
expected_fault: Incorrect or unreachable DNS server configured on the client

symptom: Internal hostname resolves to the wrong IP address.
topology_note: Internal DNS server has a stale A record for a recently re-IPed server.
show_output:
nslookup fileserver01
Address: 192.168.10.50 (old IP, server moved to .60)
expected_fault: Stale DNS A record not updated after server IP change

symptom: All external websites fail to load by name, but internal name resolution works.
topology_note: Router configured with internal DNS server only, no forwarder to external DNS.
show_output:
show running-config | include name-server
ip name-server 192.168.1.10
expected_fault: No external DNS forwarder configured; internal DNS server cannot resolve external names

symptom: PC can reach its own VLAN's gateway but cannot reach a server in another VLAN.
topology_note: L3 switch routes between VLAN 30 and VLAN 10.
show_output:
show ip route
(no route to 192.168.10.0/24 listed)
expected_fault: Missing route or disabled routing between VLAN 30 and VLAN 10

symptom: Branch office cannot reach headquarters network over a WAN link.
topology_note: Two routers connected via a serial link, static routing configured.
show_output:
show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
(no static route to 10.10.0.0/16)
expected_fault: Missing static route to the remote network on the branch router

symptom: Route to a destination exists but traffic is not using it; packets seem to take a longer path.
topology_note: Two routes exist to the same destination network with different metrics.
show_output:
show ip route 172.16.0.0
Routing entry via two paths, AD 120 (RIP) preferred over AD 90 (EIGRP) incorrectly
expected_fault: Incorrect administrative distance or misconfigured routing protocol causing suboptimal path selection

symptom: OSPF neighbors never form; routes from the neighboring router are missing.
topology_note: Two routers on the same segment, both configured for OSPF area 0.
show_output:
show ip ospf neighbor
(empty output)
show ip ospf interface
Process ID mismatch, Hello interval mismatch
expected_fault: OSPF neighbor adjacency failing due to Hello/Dead timer mismatch between routers

symptom: Server that should be reachable from one VLAN is blocked entirely, even for permitted traffic.
topology_note: ACL applied to router interface to restrict access to a finance server.
show_output:
show access-lists
ACL FINANCE-ACL
10 deny ip any any
20 permit ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any
expected_fault: ACL rule order is wrong; deny-all placed before the intended permit statement

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi devices can reach an internal server that should be isolated.
topology_note: ACL GUEST-ISOLATION intended to block VLAN 50 (guest) from VLAN 20 (internal).
show_output:
show ip interface Vlan50
(no access list configured on this interface)
expected_fault: ACL exists but was never applied to the VLAN 50 interface

symptom: Specific host can access a server; the same subnet's other hosts cannot, though they should be able to.
topology_note: ACL uses a host-specific permit statement instead of the subnet.
show_output:
show access-lists
10 permit ip host 192.168.30.5 any
20 deny ip any any
expected_fault: ACL only permits a single host instead of the full subnet as intended

symptom: Remote management access (SSH) to a router stopped working after an ACL update.
topology_note: Standard ACL applied to VTY lines for SSH restriction.
show_output:
show running-config | section line vty
access-class MGMT-ACL in
show access-lists MGMT-ACL
10 permit host 10.0.0.5 (old admin IP)
expected_fault: ACL on VTY lines references outdated admin IP, blocking current management host

symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the internet at all.
topology_note: Router configured for NAT overload (PAT) on the outside interface.

show ip nat translations
(empty)

symptom: Internet works for some internal PCs but not others.

10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255

topology_note: Static NAT/port forwarding configured for a web server.

(no static entry for 192.168.10.100)
